title: HLC timestamp u64→i64 SQLite cast silently truncates large values
description: core/src/group_log/sqlite_storage.rs:40: entry.hlc_timestamp (u64) is cast to i64 for storage. Any timestamp with bit 63 set (wall_ms > 9_223_372_036_854_775_807, i.e., after year ~292 million) would be stored as a negative i64 and read back as a nonsensical u64 > 2^63. While this will not trigger in practice this century, the absence of an assertion or range check means the bug is invisible. More importantly, the same pattern is copy-bait — if a contributor adds u64 fields to LogEntry, they will copy this cast without realising its fragility. Fix: add a compile-time static_assert or runtime assert!(entry.hlc_timestamp <= i64::MAX as u64) so the truncation is loud rather than silent.
